entities.name: PMID:27504496
observations: Chan et al. reported a trans-pQTL analysis connecting Parkinson disease risk variants with Alzheimer disease-relevant myeloid proteins in human monocytes.
The study validated the rs12456492-RIT2 to CD33 association and found a suggestive rs11060180-CCDC62/HIP1R to PTK2B association.
The authors interpreted the findings as convergence on innate immune mechanisms, not proof of a causal disease-level PD-AD interaction.

entities.name: RIT2
observations: PD risk locus rs12456492 was associated in trans with increased CD33 protein expression in human monocytes; the association was independently validated.

entities.name: CD33
observations: CD33 was one of the Alzheimer disease-relevant myeloid proteins tested and was the protein partner of the validated rs12456492-RIT2 trans-pQTL association.

entities.name: PTK2B
observations: PTK2B was among the Alzheimer disease-relevant myeloid proteins tested; rs11060180 at the CCDC62/HIP1R locus showed a strongly suggestive association with decreased PTK2B expression.

entities.name: Parkinson disease
observations: The study tested 24 Parkinson disease risk variants for trans associations with Alzheimer disease-relevant myeloid proteins.

entities.name: Alzheimer disease
observations: The study assessed Alzheimer disease-relevant myeloid proteins, including CD33, PTK2B, TREM1, TREM2, TREML2, and TYROBP, as potential trans-pQTL endpoints.
